notes: Community pack, roadmap Phase 1 candidate. 5 tracks x 10 themes x 5 grade bands = 250 blocks. Expanded by tools/generate_pack.py.

themes.theme: The risks where you actually live
themes.description: Flood maps, fault lines, storm tracks and the industrial site up the road — replacing generic fear with your address's real risk list.
themes.transfer_check: Build the ranked hazard list for your own address from official maps and records, with the evidence for each entry.

themes.theme: Seventy-two hours on your own shelf
themes.description: Water, food, light, warmth, medication — the kit that keeps a household functional for three days, sized to the people actually in it.
themes.transfer_check: Assemble or audit a real 72-hour kit for your household's actual members, including the items lists always forget.

themes.theme: The grab bag and the ninety seconds
themes.description: Documents, medications, chargers, cash — what leaves the house with you when there is no time to choose.
themes.transfer_check: Pack a real grab bag, stage it, and run the ninety-second evacuation drill with it twice.

themes.description: The out-of-area contact, the rally points, and how a separated household finds itself when networks are down or jammed.
themes.transfer_check: Write your household's communication plan on one card per person and test it with an unannounced check-in drill.

themes.description: Storage amounts per person, the sources hiding in a home, and making questionable water drinkable.
themes.transfer_check: Locate and quantify every emergency water source in a real dwelling, and demonstrate one purification method correctly.

themes.description: Light, heat, cooking and phones through an outage — running the essentials safely without the grid, and the CO line never crossed.
themes.transfer_check: Run a two-hour household blackout drill covering light, one hot meal and phone charging, with every method used safely.

themes.description: IDs, deeds, policies, prescriptions — the copies, the cloud, the sealed pouch, and proving who you are when the originals burned.
themes.transfer_check: Create the full document backup for a real household — physical copies staged, digital copies encrypted and reachable.

themes.theme: Pets and the beings who cannot pack
themes.description: Animals in evacuation: carriers, records, the shelters that take them and the ones that will not.
themes.transfer_check: Build the evacuation plan and kit for a real animal, and complete a timed load-and-go drill with it.

themes.description: The street-level map of who has skills, tools and needs — preparedness as a shared asset rather than a private bunker.
themes.transfer_check: Map your immediate neighbours' relevant skills, equipment and vulnerabilities (with consent), and agree one mutual commitment.

themes.description: Why untested plans fail, rotating supplies before they expire, and the twice-yearly hour that keeps readiness real.
themes.transfer_check: Run a full household drill against your written plan, log every failure found, and fix the worst one the same week.

tracks.name: First aid: the first ten minutes

themes.description: Danger, response, airway — why rescuers become casualties, and the look-around that comes before the kneel-down.
themes.transfer_check: Approach three staged casualty scenes, verbalising the hazard check and the decision to proceed, stage, or wait for each.

themes.description: What the call-taker needs, in what order, and the location skills (addresses, apps, landmarks) that cut minutes off arrival.
themes.transfer_check: Complete a realistic mock emergency call scored against dispatch criteria, including conveying a precise location two ways.

themes.theme: The unconscious person who is breathing
themes.description: Checking response and breathing, the recovery position, and staying until handover.
themes.transfer_check: Demonstrate the full assessment and recovery position on a live volunteer, including the monitoring you keep doing.

themes.theme: CPR and the machine on the wall
themes.description: Compressions that are hard and fast enough, rescue breaths where trained, and using an AED with its voice as your guide.
themes.transfer_check: Perform two minutes of adequate-rate, adequate-depth compressions on a manikin and run a full AED sequence to shock/no-shock.

themes.description: The universal sign, back blows and abdominal thrusts, and the differences for infants and the pregnant.
themes.transfer_check: Demonstrate the complete choking protocol on adult and infant manikins, adapting correctly for each.

themes.description: Pressure, elevation, packing and the tourniquet's honest place — stopping blood loss with what is in reach.
themes.transfer_check: Control three staged bleeds — minor, severe limb, junctional — choosing and applying the right technique for each.

themes.theme: Burns, breaks and the injuries that wait badly
themes.description: Cooling burns properly, immobilising suspected fractures, and the do-nots that make each worse.
themes.transfer_check: Manage one staged burn and one staged fracture end to end, stating what you will not do and why.

themes.description: Heart attack, stroke, seizure, severe allergy, diabetic collapse — recognising each fast and the one right action for each.
themes.transfer_check: From five scripted casualty presentations, identify each condition and perform or state its correct first response, including auto-injector use.

themes.description: Children and infants: the doses, ratios and signs that differ, and keeping a frightened child workable.
themes.transfer_check: Adapt three adult protocols correctly to a child or infant manikin, and demonstrate one calming approach while treating.

themes.theme: The kit and the kit in your head
themes.description: Building a first-aid kit that matches your life, improvising when there is none, and the refresher rhythm that keeps skills alive.
themes.transfer_check: Assemble a first-aid kit for a named context (home, car, hike), justify every item, and treat one staged injury using improvised materials only.

themes.theme: How fires actually start at home
themes.description: Cooking, smoking, chargers, candles, heaters — the ignition league table and the habits behind each entry.
themes.transfer_check: Audit a real dwelling against the top ignition causes and eliminate or mitigate every finding, with photos.

themes.theme: The alarms that buy the minutes
themes.description: Smoke and heat detector types, where each belongs, and the dead battery that undoes it all.
themes.transfer_check: Verify correct type, placement and function of every alarm in a real dwelling, and fix or specify what is missing.

themes.theme: The escape plan with two ways out
themes.description: Routes, the smoke-low crawl, the closed-door discipline and the meeting point nobody re-enters from.
themes.transfer_check: Draw the two-route escape plan for a real dwelling and run the drill with its actual occupants, timed, including the meeting point.

themes.theme: Fighting the small fire, fleeing the rest
themes.description: Extinguisher classes, the pan fire and the fire blanket, and the honest size limit where fighting stops and leaving starts.
themes.transfer_check: Match extinguisher types to five fire scenarios, demonstrate the technique (live or simulated), and state your personal stop-and-go line.

themes.description: What smoke does in minutes, why closed doors matter for hours, and surviving in a room you cannot leave.
themes.transfer_check: Demonstrate the trapped-in-room protocol — door checks, sealing, the window signal, the call — in a staged scenario.

themes.theme: The building bigger than your door
themes.description: Apartment blocks: stay-put versus evacuate policies, alarm systems, dry risers and why the policy differs by construction.
themes.transfer_check: Find and explain your own building's fire strategy, and state exactly what you would do for an alarm at 3 a.m. under it.

themes.theme: Wildfire at the edge of town
themes.description: Ember attack, defensible space, the leave-early principle and the go/no-go decision made before smoke is visible.
themes.transfer_check: Assess a real or case-study property's wildfire exposure, specify its defensible-space actions, and write its trigger-based leave plan.

themes.description: Re-entry dangers, insurance documentation, and the recovery sequence for a household that just lost its rooms.
themes.transfer_check: Produce the first-72-hours checklist for a post-fire household — safety, claims evidence, shelter, records — from a case study.

themes.theme: Fire and the very young and very old
themes.description: Who dies in home fires and why — mobility, hearing, medication sleep — and adapting alarms, plans and drills to real occupants.
themes.transfer_check: Adapt a real dwelling's fire plan for a named occupant with impaired mobility, hearing or cognition, and test the adaptation.

themes.theme: Being the workplace or venue warden
themes.description: Sweep duties, refuge points, roll calls and the authority a high-vis vest carries when everyone else is deciding to finish their coffee.
themes.transfer_check: Act as warden in a real or staged evacuation: complete the sweep, manage the reluctant, and deliver the roll-call report.

tracks.name: When the ground, water or sky turns

themes.description: Flash versus river flood, the depths that move cars and people, and the property-level defences that actually help.
themes.transfer_check: Read your address's flood risk from official maps, and state the action sequence for a warning at each of three lead times.

themes.description: What wind speeds do to roofs, trees and driving, the pre-storm hour list, and the shelter spots inside a home.
themes.transfer_check: Complete a real pre-storm property walk-around — securing, clearing, charging — and identify the safest internal refuge with reasons.

themes.description: What buildings do in shaking, the myths (doorways, running out), and the aftershock rules.
themes.transfer_check: Run the full drop-cover-hold drill in two different rooms, then perform the post-shake checks — gas, structure, exits — in order.

themes.description: Heatwave physiology, the rooms and hours that matter, and the neighbours on the checking list.
themes.transfer_check: Write and rehearse a heatwave plan for a real household including one vulnerable person's specific arrangements.

themes.theme: Cold, snow and the iced-in week
themes.description: Freezing pipes, stranded cars, carbon monoxide from improvised heating — the winter emergency's specific traps.
themes.transfer_check: Prepare a real car and home for a cold snap against a checklist, including the in-car survival kit demonstrated.

themes.description: Where lightning actually strikes people, the timing rules, and the safe and unsafe shelters.
themes.transfer_check: Given three outdoor scenarios with a building storm, state and justify the correct action and shelter for each.

themes.theme: Landslip, sinkhole and the moving ground
themes.description: Reading slopes and warning signs — cracks, leaning trees, sudden springs — and who to call before the road drops.
themes.transfer_check: Survey one real slope or cutting for instability indicators and file or draft the report to the responsible authority.

themes.description: The overturned tanker, the chemical smell, the plume — shelter-in-place done properly versus the instinct to drive through it.
themes.transfer_check: Demonstrate full shelter-in-place for a staged airborne release — sealing, ventilation off, information channel on — in your own home.

themes.theme: Warnings and the words they use
themes.description: Watch versus warning, amber versus red, sirens and cell alerts — the official vocabulary and the action each word demands.
themes.transfer_check: Match your region's actual alert levels to required actions, and show where the warnings arrive on your own devices, tested.

themes.description: Routes, timing, the full tank rule, and the decision discipline that leaves before the road jams.
themes.transfer_check: Plan two evacuation routes from your home to defined refuges, drive or trace both, and state your pre-committed leave triggers.

themes.description: Emergency services, civil protection, utilities, charities — who does what in a disaster and where the citizen fits.
themes.transfer_check: Map the actual response structure for your area — agencies, roles, activation — and identify the citizen-facing entry point of each.

themes.description: Why untasked helpers clog disasters, and the registered, trained routes by which help actually helps.
themes.transfer_check: Identify and complete registration (or its full application) with one recognised local response or resilience group.

themes.description: Look, listen, link — steadying frightened people without therapy or platitudes, and the referrals beyond your role.
themes.transfer_check: Demonstrate psychological first aid in three role-played encounters — the panicked, the numb, the searching — with correct referral for each.

themes.description: Running the hall where evacuees arrive: registration, needs triage, families kept together, and the quiet corner that matters.
themes.transfer_check: Set up and run (or fully exercise) a rest-centre reception for a staged intake of ten, with registration and needs triage completed.

themes.description: Rumour dynamics in disasters, official channels, and being the neighbour who relays what is true rather than what is loud.
themes.transfer_check: During an exercise or case study, verify three circulating claims against official sources and publish the corrected summary.

themes.description: Recording what happened — structures, utilities, needs — in the form responders and insurers can actually use.
themes.transfer_check: Complete a structured damage assessment of a staged or historical scene, producing the standard-format report.

themes.description: The registers, the door-knock lists and the housebound — how communities make sure the flood does not sort by mobility.
themes.transfer_check: Build the (consented) support map for one street's vulnerable residents and the check-in protocol that activates in an event.

themes.description: After the cameras leave: claims, rebuilding, the long tail of displacement, and pacing a community's return.
themes.transfer_check: From one documented disaster, chart its recovery timeline against needs, and identify the two support gaps that appeared at month three.

themes.description: Debriefs without blame, the report that changes procedure, and the drill updated because of what actually happened.
themes.transfer_check: Run a structured debrief of a real drill or event, extract three actionable lessons, and change one written plan accordingly.

themes.description: From prepared households to a prepared street to a town with a plan — the organising work between emergencies.
themes.transfer_check: Organise or advance one concrete community resilience action — a street meeting, a shared equipment list, a plan adopted — with evidence.
